candidate_relations.label: Invasive Ductal Carcinoma
candidate_relations.reason: Invasive ductal carcinoma is a primary breast parenchymal malignancy. The clinical picture — a young woman, 2-year slow-growing painless nodule, subcutaneous location, firm mobile mass with pleomorphic calcifications — is classic for pilomatrixoma, a benign hair-matrix tumor. IDC is a different diagnostic entity and incompatible subtype/scope, though the imaging features (BI-RADS IV, calcifications, posterior shadowing) can mimic it.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Malignant breast epithelial neoplasm vs. benign skin adnexal tumor of hair matrix origin

candidate_relations.label: Ductal Carcinoma In Situ
candidate_relations.reason: DCIS is a breast ductal epithelial in-situ malignancy. The subcutaneous, well-defined, mobile nodule with a 2-year benign clinical course in a 33-year-old is far more consistent with pilomatrixoma. DCIS is an incompatible diagnostic entity of different tissue origin and scope.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Non-invasive breast epithelial malignancy vs. benign skin adnexal tumor

candidate_relations.label: Phyllodes Tumor
candidate_relations.reason: Phyllodes tumor arises from breast stromal/fibroepithelial tissue and typically presents as a rapidly growing breast mass. The subcutaneous location, pleomorphic calcifications, and 2-year indolent course are more characteristic of pilomatrixoma. Phyllodes tumor is an incompatible entity of different tissue origin.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Fibroepithelial breast tumor vs. benign skin adnexal tumor of hair matrix origin

case_quality_flags: All three candidates are breast parenchymal neoplasms; none represents the correct diagnosis of pilomatrixoma (benign skin adnexal tumor), limiting discriminative value of the candidate set.
Subcutaneous location on ultrasound is a key differentiating feature pointing away from primary breast neoplasms toward pilomatrixoma.
